title: Tech Lead
description: WeFlex exists to increase the life expectancy and quality of life for people with a disability, people in aged care, and Australian war veterans — through access to physical fitness, allied health, and therapy supports. We've delivered over 50,000 sessions of support across our network, grown 30x over the last 2.5 years, and want to continue at a rate of 100% year on year. The seat You'll own the technology engine that powers WeFlex's end-to-end customer lifecycle — lead acquisition through retention. Today it runs across Supabase, Airtable, n8n, GoHighLevel, Zendesk, Aircall, Wavix, Xero, and our internal portals. Tomorrow it's your call to architect. You sit at the leadership table as a senior peer — reporting to our COO, partnering directly with the CEO, working alongside our Heads of Sales, CS, Marketing, and (soon) Service Providers. This is a player-coach seat. You don't just architect — you build. Then you lead a team of 5 builders to ship alongside you. Big problems we're chewing on right now: the O2C rebuild (kill Zoho), the Supabase migration (centralise source-of-truth), the AHP supervision automation that's worth ~$185k/yr in revenue if we get it right. AI augmentation is non-negotiable. We move at a pace where the only way to keep up is to have Claude / GPT / Cursor / equivalents deeply embedded in how you think and ship every day. If they're not already core to your workflow, this role isn't for you. The 5 things you'll do day-to-day: Set the technology strategy — what we build, what we migrate, what we kill. The 18-month roadmap is yours to author with the COO + CEO. Architect + build — you write the spec, then you ship the work. We don't promote you out of code. The team builds with you, not for you. Lead and grow the team — hire, performance manage, build capability, exit underperformers when needed. We have 5 builders today; you'll shape the next 10. Partner directly with CEO + COO — translate ambiguous business problems into systems that work. "Clients aren't reporting back" ? you diagnose, scope, ship. AI-augmented by default — Claude, GPT, Cursor, equivalent are part of how you ship every day, not just how you write email s. Show us your stack and a real recent build where AI was core to how you executed. What we're looking for We hire skills over credentials. AI-augmented operator (non-negotiable). Your workflow runs through Claude / GPT / Cursor — diagnosing, scoping, building, documenting. If AI is bolted on rather than core, this role won't work. Builder of systems with real artifacts. Operational systems / integrations / automations you've shipped end-to-end. Portfolio over CV. Show us the code, the flows, the Looms. Architectural judgment at scale. You've made build-vs-buy / migrate-vs-rebuild calls. You've owned a platform decision and can defend it. You think in trade-offs, not absolutes. Track record leading a small tech team. Hiring, performance management, capability building, hard conversations. We have 5 builders; you'll d ---------- who stays, who grows, who goes. Translates ambiguous executive briefs into shipped systems. When the CEO says "we need to know which clients are at risk" — you diagnose, scope, build, ship. You don't wait for the perfect spec. Degree, years-of-experience, prior industry — all signals, not gates. If your work speaks, your CV doesn't have to be conventional. What this role does NOT involve ? Marketing tech / GHL funnel design ? marketing team owns this ? Direct customer service ? CS team owns Zendesk as a product ? Heavy DevOps / infrastructure architecture ? we're a small remote team running on managed services ? Mobile / native app development ? we run web + portal stack Compensation PHP 90,000–220,000 per month depending on experience and demonstrated capability Fully remote, AEST-aligned working hours Career trajectory: This is the technology counterpart to our COO-track seat. For the right person, ownership expands as we scale — through Head of Engineering and beyond — as WeFlex grows. To apply Submit your application here: ---------- The application has two parts: Part 1 — Application form Your CV Portfolio link (GitHub, Loom library, case studies, live systems you've built) 3 short written answers Notice period + salary expectation Part 2 — Build task A real WeFlex scenario with sample data. You build a working artifact and record a short Loom walking us through your thinking, your tool choice, and your AI workflow. No time limit — we score the quality of the build, not how fast you finished. Full briefing pack is provided when you start the application. We hire builders, not talkers. The build task is the highest-weight signal in our process.

job_title: n8n / API Developer for FieldPulse + CTM + AI Voice Intake Automation
description: Project Overview I am looking for an experienced automation/API developer to build Phase 1 of a field service intake automation system. This project involves CallTrackingMetrics, FieldPulse, n8n, webhooks, APIs, customer lookup, job creation, alerts, and AI voice intake. The goal of Phase 1 is not full dispatch or scheduling. The goal is to create a reliable intake system that captures qualified service requests, creates or updates the correct customer/job record, and sends alerts so a human can review and take over. Phase 1 Scope The first build should include these modules: Module 1 — Intake / Webhook Receiver Receive incoming call/contact/intake data through webhook or API. This may come from CallTrackingMetrics, an AI voice agent, web form, chatbot, or test payload. The workflow should capture and structure fields such as: Customer name Phone number Service location / city / ZIP Vehicle or equipment description Service issue Urgency Roadside / safety status if applicable Lead source / tracking number if available Call summary or transcript if available Module 2 — AI Voice Intake Assistant Set up or integrate an AI voice intake assistant that collects required intake information. The voice agent must act only as an intake assistant. It should not diagnose, estimate, schedule, dispatch, or promise response times. The voice agent should identify whether the caller is a qualified service request, out of area, sales/spam, existing customer follow-up, or needs human follow-up. Module 3 — FieldPulse Customer / Job Record Creation Use FieldPulse API or approved integration method to: Search for an existing customer before creating a new one Avoid duplicate customer records when possible Create or update customer information Create a job, lead, or service request record Attach relevant intake details, notes, call summary, source, and urgency Module 4 — Alerts and Human Review Output Send alerts when a qualified service request is received. Minimum alert output should include: Customer name Phone number City / ZIP / location Vehicle or equipment Service issue Urgency Roadside / safety status FieldPulse customer/job link if available Intake summary Whether the record was created, updated, or flagged for review Alerts may be sent by SMS, email , FieldPulse notification, or another agreed method. Important Rules This is Phase 1 only. The system should not automatically dispatch technicians, schedule appointments, give price estimates, diagnose mechanical problems, order parts, or promise arrival times. Human review remains part of the process. Required Experience Please apply only if you have experience with some or all of the following: n8n workflow automation Webhooks and REST APIs CRM or field-service software API integrations Customer lookup before creating new records Job, lead, or service request creation through API CallTrackingMetrics, FieldPulse, or similar platforms AI voice agents such as Vapi, Retell, Twilio, Bland, or similar Error handling, logging, and workflow documentation Preferred First Step I would like to start with a small fixed-price test module before the full build. The test module should prove that you can receive a sample intake payload, apply qualification logic, check for an existing customer, prepare a FieldPulse-ready record, and send a structured alert. Please include in your response: Relevant n8n/API/webhook projects you have built Whether you have worked with FieldPulse, CallTrackingMetrics, or similar platforms Whether you have built AI voice intake agents Your recommended approach for Phase 1 Estimated hours and cost for the first test module

title: Founding Full Stack Engineer for nonprofit and growing startup (dual company)
job_title: Founding Full Stack Engineer for nonprofit and growing startup (dual company)
description: About Us Our company is the cultural infrastructure layer for upstream youth mental health. We build fan-native experiences — like a post-concert QR scan that lets fans capture an emotional ---------- nt and get a beautiful shareable artifact back — that quietly deliver evidence-based protective factors to young people in the language they already speak. We're building this from a Lovable prototype to a real platform, and we need a founding engineer to own the build. What this person actually does > Owns the technical build of our first product end-to-end — from the fan-facing web experience to the back-end data layer to the SMS/email delivery system that returns fans' notes to them months later. > Takes the Lovable prototype as the spec, rebuilds it properly, ships it to production, and then keeps building all our upcoming other tools, and the data infrastructure that holds it all together. > This is not a "code monkey" role. This person is making architectural decisions that determine whether our company can scale to millions of fans and dozens of partners (or whether we hit a wall in eighteen months and have to rebuild from scratch). > They need to think about privacy, consent flows for minors, data architecture for longitudinal records, partner integrations, and the AI/ML layer that comes next. Day-to-day responsibilities > Rebuild our first (flagship) tool from the Lovable prototype as a production web app > Build the identity layer (phone number / email -based, not app-based) that lets fans be recognized across surfaces > Set up the data architecture: every fan interaction stored in a way that's queryable, longitudinal, and IRB-clean for future research > Build the SMS and email delivery system (i.e Twilio + a transactional email provider like Postmark or Resend) > Build the partner-facing admin/dashboard so future partners can deploy our company's tools and see anonymized aggregate data > Set up privacy infrastructure from day one — consent flows, data minimization, COPPA-compliant flows for minors, deletion-on-request > Work directly with the graphic designer to translate designs into production-quality UI > Make decisions on the tech stack, hosting, deployment, monitoring — and document them so future hires can ramp in > Eventually: integrate the AI/ML layer that powers the protective-factor model

job_title: TECHNICAL SUPPORT ENGINEER (AI-ASSISTED TROUBLESHOOTING, INTEGRATIONS, APIs) - US HOURS | G2 AWARD-WINNING US COMPANY
description: Remote (Philippines) | Full-Time | High-Ownership Career Role | US Hours Required Most support roles are a dead end. This one isn't. You're good at what you do — probably too good for where you are. You troubleshoot issues other people can't figure out. You communicate clearly when things are on fire. You take ownership of problems and drive them to resolution while everyone else is still triaging. And you're stuck. The title doesn't match the work. The growth path is vague. The team doesn't challenge you. The company doesn't see what you're capable of. We do. TOKEN OF TRUST — WHAT WE DO AND WHY IT MATTERS Token of Trust is a G2-recognized, award-winning identity verification platform. Our clients are regulated ecommerce businesses across the US who rely on us to verify real consumers, block fraud, and stay compliant — in industries where getting it wrong means legal exposure, lost revenue, or both. When checkout verification breaks on a customer's live site at 2pm on a Tuesday, we're the team that figures out why and fixes it. We ship weekly. Our last team-wide compensation increase was three months ago. When something breaks, the whole team rallies — not because they have to, but because they care. The engineering team builds the product. The operations team makes sure it works in the real world. This role is the technical backbone of that operations team. THE ROLE We're hiring a Technical Support Engineer to own technical problem-solving across our product and customer integrations. You will: * be the first person to dig into hard technical problems — the ones that require real investigation, not just a script * troubleshoot complex integration issues across WordPress, WooCommerce, Shopify, BigCommerce, and custom platforms * devise and test workarounds for customers, then give the product team clear, actionable information on what's wrong and how to fix it * configure and deploy our product across customer environments — and lead go-lives independently over time * write the playbooks that make recurring issues faster to resolve and easier to delegate * catch product issues before they reach customers through disciplined QA and regression testing * use AI tools daily as a force multiplier — for research, troubleshooting, analysis, and documentation This is not entry-level support. This is not a developer role. This is the kind of role where a strong technical support engineer becomes indispensable — and gets recognized for it. You do not need to write code for this role. Developer experience helps because it gives you intuition for how systems work, but what we need is someone who can configure existing products, read what a system is telling them, and explain it clearly. The ability to understand a system matters more than the ability to build one. WHO THIS IS FOR You're a strong fit if you come from technical support, implementation support, support engineering, QA, or technical operations — and you want a role where your ceiling is set by your performance, not your title. You should be: * the person your team already escalates hard problems to * someone who writes things down so the next person doesn't have to re-investigate * comfortable with structured data, API documentation, and browser dev tools * already using AI tools in your work and seeing the leverage they provide * looking for a team that will challenge you, trust you, and give you room to grow WHAT YOU'LL OWN Technical Support Leadership (Primary Focus) You'll be the senior technical resource on the Operations team — the person who handles issues that require real judgment. * triage, reproduce, and drive resolution of technical support issues * distinguish between user error, configuration issues, integration problems, and product defects * find workarounds for customers while permanent fixes are in progress * gather the right evidence before escalating to Development — so engineers can act immediately, not investigate from scratch * build and improve technical support playbooks so recurring issues can be delegated to the rest of the team * personally drive the hardest, most ambiguous, or most business-critical issues to closure * communicate clearly with customers and internal teams so the right people stay informed without unnecessary noise Where This Role Grows We're a small company, so we promise you will not get bored. Depending upon how quickly you learn, and how broad your interests, you'll be involved in other areas. As you build trust, you'll be invited to expand into spaces where your skills naturally lead, including but not limited to: * **Go-Lives and Integration Enablement** — as the strongest troubleshooter on the ops team, you'll naturally get pulled into the most important and complex client launches. You'll configure plugins and integrations across WordPress, WooCommerce, Shopify, and BigCommerce. You'll join screen-share sessions with customers to resolve setup issues. Over time, you could lead go-lives independently. The core skill is configuring existing systems correctly — not writing new code. * **QA and Release Confidence** — you'll be among the first to test cool new features, find nasty defects, tell development exactly what's wrong, validate fixes before production, and over time help automate regression testing. The goal: we catch issues before customers do. * **Automation and Structured Operations** — you'll use AI with our APIs, logs, and structured data (JSON, YAML, CSV) and source code to investigate and confirm behavior. You'll build lightweight scripts, prompts, checklists, and internal tools that make the whole team faster. You'll help turn recurring patterns into systems so the organization gets stronger every month. title: Full-Stack Engineer
description: If you want to be part of a growing small business that's building with AI and shipping fast, you'll like it here. If you're tired of being one of a hundred engineers maintaining a service you didn't design, this is the opposite. You own the whole stack. You pick your tools. Your work ships in days, not quarters. About: The Mousepad Company is a small US-based DTC brand. We make premium gaming and desk mousepads, printed in-house in California. The team is lean and the owner is hands-on. We ship constantly. The job: You are the owner's technical right hand. Build and maintain our internal app (OPPY) and our customer-facing creator studio (MPCO Studio). You are the only software person on the team. You ship features, integrations, dashboards, and automations: whatever the business needs that week. We do not have a Jira full of cleanly-scoped tickets waiting for you. You help us figure out what to build next. What you do: Phase 1, OPPY (first 30 to 60 days): Take a list of feature requests and ship them. Make the app more efficient, then faster, then more beautiful, in that order. Examples of what we'll ask for: "I click this button and this data shows up." "This page loads in 4 seconds, get it under 1." "This workflow takes 5 clicks, get it to 2." Phase 2, MPCO Studio: Custom mousepad designer web app. Think Figma but exporting creates a print file. More details to be discussed later. Ongoing: Slack custom commands. Notion to Shopify integrations. ---------- to Creator Studio integrations. Financial dashboards. Helping the team use AI better. Internal tools that do not exist yet. When you run out of assigned work, you find what is slow or broken and fix it. Compensation: Monthly salary, paid via Wise. Long-term role. Quarterly performance review with potential raises for top performers. What we need from you: You ship fast and constantly. Your last side project shipped in a weekend, not a year. You live in modern AI coding tools (Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, similar) and have opinions on which is best for what. You are a generalist. You can build a Slack bot in the morning, debug a Shopify webhook at lunch, and ship a financial dashboard in the afternoon. You read a stack you have never used and ship in it within a week. You self-direct. Nobody assigns you tickets. You find what matters and do it. Strong written English. Willing to work West Coast US hours. Nice to have: Built something with creator economy or affiliate program tech before. Built a design canvas or image-generation tool before. Shopify, Next.js, Prisma, PostgreSQL, Railway on your résumé. Slack bots, ---------- bots, or Notion integrations on your résumé. A note up front: AI is a tool you live in for this role, so we don't ban it in your application. But generic AI-generated answers are filtered out immediately. Use AI to help you express yourself, not to do the thinking. To apply, send: Ship proof. Link us to something you built recently, alone. Could be a side project, a tool, an integration, anything that ships. Tell us in 3 sentences how long it took and what tools you used to build it. Workflow Loom. Record a 90-second Loom screen-share of your actual coding workflow. Show us your editor, your AI tools, how you move. Don't perform. Just show us what a normal afternoon looks like. Generalist test. Pick one of these three and tell us in plain English how you'd build it. No code, just your approach. (a) A Slack command that pulls last week's blended MER from a PostgreSQL database. (b) A Shopify webhook that auto-creates a Notion task every time a refund over $100 is processed. (c) A creator dashboard showing creator earnings, active design submissions, and approval status.

You will own the client onboarding process after their website is built, ensuring they are fully trained and integrated into our GoHighLevel (GHL) ecosystem. Your goal is to build relationships with clients while designing and maintaining the automation engines that drive their business—from review requests and database reactivation to "voi cemail bombs" and unified communication pipelines. ## What You’ll Do ### Client Onboarding & Account Management Lead the Handoff: Take ownership of the client relationship immediately after the website build is complete. Automated Outreach: Build and manage workflows for automated review requests, referral generation, and repeat appointment reminders. Database Reactivation: Execute "voi cemail bombs" and text/email blasts to send targeted mass communications to leads and customer lists. Phone Systems: Configure VoIP systems for clients, ensuring call tracking, recording, and metrics are functioning correctly. ### Marketing Campaigns & Reporting Lifecycle Marketing: Create and manage email campaigns tailored to specific stages of the sales funnel, including seasonal blasts and monthly newsletters. Chat Widgets: Install and configure website chat widgets for real-time lead capture. Reporting: Design customized dashboards inside GHL that provide clients with clear visibility into their ROI and KPIs. Social & Content: Assist with social media planning for repeat content and ensure consistent messaging across all channels. ### What Success Looks Like (Accountability) Smooth Onboarding: Clients feel confident and supported during the transition from "build" to "live." System Uptime: Automations trigger correctly, and communication channels (VoIP, Chat, SMS) remain active without error. title: Claude Code Expert - Vibe Coder
description: Location: Fully Remote (PH) Schedule: Monday–Friday, 9:00 AM–5:00 PM EST (with flexibility as needed for client impact events) About T3 Tech Partners T3 Tech Partners is the team MSPs rely on when challenges exceed Tier 2 or internal expertise. We operate as a Fractional Tier 3 partner, delivering advanced Microsoft 365, cloud, security, and AI engineering expertise to MSPs supporting diverse client environments. We build and operate AI-powered applications that automate the most time-consuming parts of MSP work — tenant management, reporting, security reviews, and migrations. Our stack runs on DigitalOcean and is powered by the Anthropic API. Role Overview We are seeking a senior AI Application Engineer to design, build, and operate production applications powered by the Anthropic API. You'll own the backend services, integrations, and infrastructure that turn Claude into reliable, multi-tenant tooling for MSPs and their clients. This is a hands-on engineering role. You'll write the code, ship the features, deploy the services, watch the dashboards, and tune the prompts. You should be equally comfortable architecting a tool-use loop against the Messages API, debugging a Node service on a DigitalOcean droplet, designing a Postgres schema for multi-tenant isolation, and explaining cost trade-offs to leadership. Key Responsibilities Anthropic API & AI Application Development (Core Focus) Design and build production applications on top of the Anthropic API — Messages, tool use, streaming, prompt caching, batch processing, the Files API, and MCP connectors where appropriate. Architect multi-turn agentic workflows, tool-use loops, and structured-output pipelines that hold up against real customer data, not just demos. Implement robust prompt and context engineering practices: system prompt design, dynamic context assembly, retrieval, and output validation. Build evals and regression suites so prompt and model changes don't silently degrade behavior in production. Optimize for cost and latency at scale: prompt caching strategies, model selection (Haiku vs. Sonnet vs. Opus), batch processing for non-realtime workloads, and token budgets per tenant. Implement guardrails: input validation, output verification, rate limiting, abuse detection, and safe handling of customer data. Backend & API Engineering Build and maintain backend services in Python and/or Node.js/TypeScript, exposing clean REST or RPC APIs to internal tools, partner integrations, and end-user products. Design multi-tenant data models in PostgreSQL with proper tenant isolation, encryption, and audit logging. Integrate with the Microsoft Graph, Google Workspace Admin SDK, and MSP platform APIs (SuperOps, Hudu, and similar) to feed Claude with the right context and act on its outputs. Implement authentication and authorization (OAuth 2.0, OIDC, app registrations, service principals) across Microsoft and Google identity ecosystems. Design background job systems, queues, and webhook handlers for long-running AI workflows. DigitalOcean Infrastructure & Operations Own the deployment, scaling, and operations of our application stack on DigitalOcean — Droplets, App Platform, Managed Databases (Postgres, Redis), Spaces, VPCs, and load balancers. Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions or similar) for automated testing, deployment, and rollback. Containerize services with Docker; manage configuration, secrets, and environment promotion across dev/staging/prod. Implement observability: structured logging, metrics, request tracing, and AI-specific telemetry (token usage, latency, eval scores, cost per tenant). Maintain backup, disaster recovery, and security baselines for production workloads. Harden services for the realities of running customer-data-handling apps: TLS, secret rotation, dependency hygiene, and least-privilege IAM. Integration with MSP & Microsoft 365 Workflows Build integrations against the Microsoft Graph and Google Workspace Admin SDK to power AI features over real tenant data — mailboxes, drives, identities, devices, and policies. Develop and maintain PowerShell components where Microsoft tooling demands it, and bridge cleanly back to the main backend. Support T3's product work (including T3nant Wiz) and internal MSP delivery tooling with shared services and libraries. Work with the rest of the team to identify high-leverage automation opportunities and ship them. Engineering Discipline Write clean, tested, reviewed code. Treat AI-generated code as a draft to be read, not output to be trusted. Maintain meaningful test coverage — unit, integration, and AI-output evals. Participate in code review, design discussions, and post-i ---------- reviews. Document architecture, runbooks, and operational procedures so the team can support what you build. Availability & Support Expectations Standard working hours are 9:00 AM–5:00 PM EST. Some flexibility is required for production deployments, i ---------- response, or critical client work outside normal hours. This role is not on-call, but responsiveness during critical events is expected. Qualifications Required Experience 5+ years of hands-on backend or full-stack engineering experience shipping production applications. Demonstrable production experience building applications on the Anthropic API or directly comparable LLM APIs (OpenAI, Google Gemini, AWS Bedrock). You should be able to walk us through real systems you've built — tool-use loops, streaming UIs, evals, cost optimizations, and the trade-offs behind each. Strong Python or Node.js/TypeScript for backend service development. Solid PostgreSQL experience: schema design, query tuning, migrations, multi-tenant patterns. Production experience deploying and operating services on DigitalOcean (or directly comparable IaaS — AWS, Azure, GCP, Linode, Hetzner). Strong Linux, shell, and command-line fluency. title: DevOps Engineer
description: If your instinct when something breaks is to fix the pipeline before fixing the symptom — this role was built for you. To apply please fill out the application form here: ---------- /bepartofourteam. About the company We're a family-owned business with all-local Philippines leadership and team. We've been 100% work-from-home since day one — not a pandemic pivot. We've grown by valuing our people, building long-term relationships, and doing great work for great clients. The Role You're not here to deploy code and move on. You're here to make sure the systems that deliver that code are reliable, secure, automated, and continuously improving. We're looking for a DevOps Engineer who thinks in pipelines, not tasks. You'll own the infrastructure that keeps our development and client environments running — CI/CD pipelines, Linux systems, cloud platforms, monitoring, and security. When something breaks, you find the root cause. When something works, you ask how to make it more reliable, more automated, and less dependent on human intervention next time. The Mindset We're Looking For The best DevOps engineers we've worked with share a few traits: They treat manual processes as technical debt. If something requires a human to do it repeatedly, their instinct is to eliminate that dependency — not just document it They take ownership. From the ---------- nt an infrastructure problem is theirs, it's theirs until it's resolved, documented, and hardened against happening again They think in systems. They don't just fix what's broken — they ask what else could break, and why, and build accordingly They communicate clearly. Status, blockers, and deployment risks are shared openly — before being asked for They keep learning. The DevOps landscape moves fast. Twelve months from now they know more than they do today — because they made sure of it Who Thrives Here People who are technically sharp, operationally minded, and genuinely excited by the challenge of building infrastructure that just works. You don't wait to be handed a list of things to automate — you find them. You're comfortable with ambiguity, resourceful under pressure, and you care more about system reliability than staying in a defined lane. We're a growing MSP, which means not every pipeline is optimized and not every process is documented yet. For the right engineer, that's not a warning — it's the opportunity to build things the right way from the ground up. What You'll Do You'll walk into an environment where development pipelines, Linux infrastructure, cloud systems, and client integrations all need an engineer who can own them end-to-end. Your job isn't just to keep things running — it's to make them run better, more reliably, and with less human intervention every month. That looks like: Designing, building, and maintaining CI/CD pipelines that make deployments fast, reliable, and repeatable — so shipping code is a non-event, not a risk Managing and administering Linux servers (Ubuntu, CentOS, Debian) across development and client environments — knowing these systems well enough to troubleshoot them at any layer Administering web servers (Nginx, Apache) and databases — keeping them performant, secure, and maintainable Implementing client-requested integrations — understanding what's being asked, translating it into a reliable technical solution, and delivering it cleanly Conducting root cause analysis on production errors — not just fixing what's visible, but understanding what allowed it to happen and building the safeguard that prevents it Building scripts and automation (Bash required; Python and PHP a plus) that eliminate repetitive manual work from the team's daily operations Monitoring infrastructure, resource utilization, and security events — building alerting systems that catch problems before they become i ---------- Designing and enforcing DevSecOps practices — making security a built-in part of the pipeline, not an afterthought Working with cloud platforms and virtualization — managing hypervisors and cloud service providers with the confidence of someone who's done it in production What We're Looking For Proven experience in Linux server administration (Ubuntu, CentOS, Debian) — you know these systems well enough to manage, troubleshoot, and optimize them without a guide Hands-on CI/CD experience — you've built and maintained real pipelines, not just used them; you know what makes a deployment safe and what makes it a liability Strong version control administration — Git, remote repositories, branching strategies, code review workflows; you manage these with intention, not just habit Web server administration experience — Nginx and Apache, configuration, performance tuning, and troubleshooting Database administration experience — you can manage database servers, optimize queries, and keep data environments healthy Bash scripting proficiency (required) — you write automation that works, that others can read, and that makes the team faster; Python and PHP experience is a plus Solid cloud computing and virtualization experience — working with hypervisors and cloud service providers (AWS, GCP, Azure, or equivalent) in real production environments Infrastructure and event monitoring experience — you build alerting systems that surface the right information at the right time, not noise Understanding of DevSecOps — you treat security as part of the build, not something bolted on at the end Strong diagnostic skills — you find the root cause of a production issue, not just the fastest path to closing the ticket Self-directed once you understand the environment — but you ask smart questions early to get there Honest communicator — you surface risks and blockers clearly and early, even when the news isn't good Long-term mindset — you want to build something that lasts, not move on when things get complex How Onboarding Works (And How That Changes) We're honest about how we work with new tea ---------- mbers. In your first weeks and months, you'll have real hands-on support from the team. We'll work closely with you to understand our infrastructure, our standards, our tools, and how we operate. We expect questions — and we'll give you the time to learn. As you show what you can do — and you will — that involvement steps back quickly. Trust grows fast here. People who demonstrate ownership, judgment, and quality work earn autonomy quickly. People who consistently deliver end up with significant latitude to shape the infrastructure, the pipelines, and how we build. We don't want to over-direct people who don't need it. But we also don't believe in throwing someone in without context and calling it autonomy. We earn each other's trust through real work — then we get out of the way. What Success Looks Like At three months: You have a clear picture of the infrastructure landscape — what's healthy, what's fragile, and what needs to be rebuilt. At least one significant manual process has been automated. Your documentation is already what the team references. At six months: Deployments are more reliable and less stressful than when you joined. Monitoring is catching problems before they become i ---------- . The team is spending less time on reactive firefighting and more time building. At twelve months: The infrastructure is measurably more stable, secure, and automated than before you joined. You've built systems the team depends on — and you're already identifying the next layer of improvement. ---------- is investing in your next step. How We Work You won't be micromanaged. We trust our people to do great work and we give them the space to do it. There's real work to be done — clients and internal teams depend on the infrastructure you manage — but we understand that doing meaningful work means making decisions, and sometimes those decisions won't be right on the first try. That's how we find the right path. We don't punish thoughtful mistakes. We learn from them and move forward. We're a growing MSP, so not every pipeline is optimized and not every process is documented yet. That's part of why we need someone like you — to help us build the infrastructure, automations, and systems that make us better as we grow. This Role Is Not for You If: You need a defined list of tasks to know what to work on You deploy the fix without asking what caused the failure You treat documentation and runbooks as someone else's job You're comfortable with fragile systems as long as they're currently running Your outside commitments regularly affect your availability and focus You're looking for a low-pressure remote role with predictable, well-defined work There's no judgment in that list — it's just not the environment. We'd rather be honest now than waste each other's time. What We Offer Competitive salary based on experience 100% remote — no corporate commute, ever Weekly pay Tech and internet allowance Paid vacation leave HMO Access to the latest AI tools (Claude, Code, and more) to work smarter and automate more Career growth

title: Senior IT Engineer
description: Senior IT Engineer Prevent problems before they happen. Automate what shouldn’t be done twice. Do great work with great clients — and earn the autonomy to do it your way. To apply please fill out the application form here: ---------- /bepartofourteam. About the Company We’re a family-owned business with all-local Philippines leadership and team. We’ve been 100% work-from-home since day one — not a pandemic pivot. We’ve grown by valuing our people, building long-term relationships, and doing great work for great clients. The Role You’re not here to close tickets faster. You’re here to make sure the same problem doesn’t come back — and ideally, to catch it before it ever reaches a ticket queue. We’re looking for a Senior IT Engineer who thinks like an automator and operator first, a firefighter second. You’ll handle complex Tier 2/3 escalations when they arise, but your real work is building the systems, automations, and processes that prevent issues from happening in the first place. You’ll own client environments, lead from the front technically, and raise the standard of the team around you. The Mindset We’re Looking For The best engineers we’ve worked with share a few traits: They hate doing the same thing twice. If they fix something manually, their next thought is: “How do I make sure no one — including me — has to do this again?” They take ownership. From the ---------- nt a problem is theirs, it’s theirs until it’s fully resolved, documented, and won’t come back They think upstream. Instead of asking “how do I fix this faster?” they ask “why is this happening, and how do I prevent it?” They communicate clearly. Status, blockers, and resolutions are shared openly — before being asked for They keep learning. Twelve months from now, they know more than they do today — without anyone telling them to Who Thrives Here People who want to do genuinely good work, be trusted by their team, and build something that lasts. We move fast and hold a high bar — but we’ve also built an environment where people are respected, given real ownership, and invested in over time. Those things aren’t in conflict here. We’re a growing MSP, which means not every process is fully documented and not every system is perfect yet. For the right engineer, that’s not a problem — it’s the opportunity to shape how we operate, not just execute within it. What You’ll Do You’ll walk into a fast-moving MSP environment where clients depend on you and junior engineers look to you. Your job isn’t just to solve the problem in front of you — it’s to make sure the team and the environment are better because you were there. That looks like: Serving as the Tier 3 escalation point for complex issues across servers, networks, cloud platforms, and endpoint security — diagnosing root causes, not patching symptoms Proactively auditing client environments to catch risks, vulnerabilities, and inefficiencies before they become i ---------- Building monitoring, alerting, and automation that catches problems early — or eliminates them entirely Leading infrastructure projects end-to-end — cloud migrations, M365 deployments, network overhauls, security implementations — from scoping through delivery Writing and maintaining PowerShell scripts that turn repetitive manual tasks into automated, reliable processes Mentoring junior engineers so that when they come to you stuck, they leave sharper and more capable — not more dependent Communicating clearly with clients and vendors — technical enough to be credible, human enough to build trust Documenting everything you touch so clearly that others can build on it without asking you a single question What We’re Looking For 5+ years of IT experience, minimum 2 in an MSP or multi-client environment — you’ve seen enough environments to know what good looks like Deep proficiency in Windows Server (2016–2022), Active Directory, DNS/DHCP, Group Policy, and virtualization (VMware/Hyper-V) — you don’t need to look up the basics Strong networking fundamentals — routing, switching, VLANs, firewall management (SonicWall, Fortinet, or Meraki); you can trace a problem through the stack Solid Microsoft 365 and Azure experience (AZ-104 level or equivalent) — you know the platform well enough to administer, troubleshoot, and advise clients on it PowerShell scripting proficiency — you write scripts that work, that others can read, and that solve real operational problems Hands-on experience with RMM and PSA platforms (Datto, HaloPSA, NinjaRMM, or equivalent) — you know how to use your tools, not just log into them VOIP support experience (3CX or similar) — you can configure, troubleshoot, and advise without escalating Strong diagnostic skills — you find root causes, not just the closest available fix Natural mentor — you make the engineers around you better without making them dependent on you Self-directed once you understand the environment — but you ask smart questions early to get there Honest communicator — you say what’s happening clearly and on time, even when the update isn’t good news Long-term mindset — you want to grow with a company, not job-hop How Onboarding Works (And How That Changes) We’re honest about how we work with new tea ---------- mbers. In your first weeks and months, you’ll have real hands-on support from the team. We’ll work closely with you to understand client environments, our standards, our tools, and how we operate. We expect questions — and we’ll give you the time to learn. As you show what you can do — and you will — that involvement steps back quickly. Trust grows fast here. People who demonstrate ownership, judgment, and quality work earn autonomy quickly. People who consistently deliver end up with significant latitude to shape their work, their tools, and their clients’ environments. We don’t want to over-direct people who don’t need it. But we also don’t believe in throwing someone in without context and calling it autonomy. We earn each other’s trust through real work — then we get out of the way. What Success Looks Like At 3 months: You’ve taken full ownership of your client environments Escalations from junior engineers are getting cleaner answers — and fewer of them You know where the gaps are and you’ve already started closing them At 6 months: Recurring issues in your client environments are measurably down — because you automated them away, not just resolved them faster Your documentation and scripts are becoming what the team reaches for first At 12 months: Clients notice the quality difference The “this issue again?” ---------- nts have dropped significantly Junior engineers are visibly sharper from working with you You’ve shaped how we operate — and the business is investing in your next step How We Work You won’t be micromanaged. We trust our people to do great work and we give them the space to do it. There’s real work to be done — clients depend on us — but we understand that doing meaningful work means making decisions, and sometimes those decisions won’t be right on the first try. That’s how we find the right path. We don’t punish thoughtful mistakes. We learn from them and move forward. We’re a growing MSP, so not every system is perfect yet and not every process is documented. That’s part of why we need someone like you — to help us build the automations, processes, and systems that make us better as we grow. This Role Is Not for You If: You need step-by-step direction to know what to do next You fix the symptom and move on without asking why You treat documentation as someone else’s responsibility You’re comfortable letting a ticket sit without following through Your outside commitments regularly affect your availability and focus You’re looking for a stable, low-pressure remote job with a predictable routine There’s no judgment in that list — it’s just not the environment. We’d rather be honest now than waste each other’s time. What We Offer Competitive salary based on experience 100% remote — no corporate commute, ever Weekly pay via Wise direct deposit Tech and internet allowance Paid vacation leave HMO Access to the latest AI tools (Claude, Cursor, and more) to work smarter and automate more Career growth opportunities in a fast-moving, systems-focused environment

description: Job Title: Build Searchable Lecture Archive — Python Developer with AI/Search Experience To confirm you read this posting, please start your reply with the word "Miller." About the Project We are Simchas Hachaim Publishing (a division of Yeshiva Gedolah Bais Yisroel), and we have an archive of approximately 2,000 lectures by Rabbi Avigdor Miller. The lectures have been transcribed into Word documents (.docx) and are stored in a Dropbox folder. We need a developer to build a search engine that lets our internal staff search the full archive by topic and keyword. Please note: this is religious Jewish material (Torah lectures). Applicants should be comfortable working with this subject matter. What Needs to Be Built A working search engine over ~2,000 .docx transcripts with the following requirements: Core functionality: Semantic/topic search — e.g., "everywhere Rabbi Miller discussed bitachon during financial hardship" — using AI embeddings so search works even where transcripts have errors Exact keyword search — for finding specific words or phrases Results show snippets with context plus the source lecture number and a link to open the original .docx Filter by lecture number or date if metadata is available Important requirements: The system must work on the current imperfect transcripts (some Hebrew, Yiddish, and Aramaic terms are mangled). Later, a scholar will go through and correct the transcripts, and the search engine must automatically re-index updated files (drop-in folder model — no manual import each time). Fully automated ingestion — when a transcript is updated or a new one added to the folder, the system picks it up without manual work. Data ownership — all transcripts and the search index must remain in formats we own and can export. No platform lock-in. Internal use first — for SHP staff. Public-facing access may come later, so build with that in mind but don't over-engineer for it now. Future audio linking — eventually we want search results to link to the original audio recording of that lecture. Not required in v1, but please structure the data so this can be added later. Technical preferences (open to your recommendations): Python-based A vector database (Pinecone, Chroma, Weaviate, or similar) for semantic search A simple web interface (Flask, FastAPI, or Streamlit is fine) — does not need to be fancy, just functional Should run either on a local server or affordable cloud hosting; please advise on the cheapest sustainable hosting option Deliverables Working Python script(s) that ingest all .docx files from a Dropbox folder, parse them, and build/update the search index automatically A simple web interface staff can use to search and view results Clear written documentation: how to run it, how to update it, how to add new transcripts A 30-minute video walkthrough of the system at the end of the project All source code delivered to us (GitHub repo or zipped files) What I Need From You in Your Application Examples of similar work — search engines, document indexing, RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) systems, or similar projects you've built Your proposed approach — briefly, which tools/stack would you recommend and why Estimated timeline to a working v1 Your availability — hours per week and overlap with U.S. Eastern Time Experience with AI/LLM tools — OpenAI API, Anthropic API, embeddings, vector databases Nice to Have Experience with Hebrew/Yiddish/Aramaic text processing Experience building tools for religious or academic archives Familiarity with Dropbox API

description: ============================================================ MICROSOFT POWER PLATFORM AUTOMATION ENGINEER (Contractor, 30-40 Hours/Week, 100% Remote, Philippines) ============================================================ We're on the lookout for a Microsoft Power Platform Automation Engineer to join our startup. This is a fully remote contractor role of roughly 30 to 40 hours per week. We work in sprint cycles and meet briefly each day for a team huddle, so we need someone whose hours overlap with U.S. business hours for these touchpoints. We're hiring in the Philippines. If you're someone who brings a positive attitude to your work, is hardworking, and is excited about being part of a growing team, we'd love to hear from you! ============================================================ COMPANY OVERVIEW ============================================================ We specialize in helping law firms streamline their operations with automations, especially through AI. We're a Google Workspace company in the middle of pivoting to Microsoft 365, which means you'll be joining at a pivotal ---------- nt where you can help shape how we build things going forward. As a startup, we're still building our systems and processes from the ground up, which means you'll have the chance to make a real impact right from the start. Joining us now means being part of a close, collaborative team where every voice matters. ============================================================ WHAT DOES A MICROSOFT POWER PLATFORM AUTOMATION ENGINEER DO? ============================================================ Your main role will be to build and manage advanced automation workflows for our Microsoft 365 law firm clients using Power Automate, Azure (including Azure OpenAI, Azure AI Content Understanding, Azure AI Document Intelligence, and Azure Functions), Microsoft Graph API, and custom connectors. You'll read and implement solutions directly from developer documentation. That includes the documentation for whichever practice management, billing, e-signature, document, or messaging platform our clients happen to use (Practice Panther, LawPay, and similar tools come up regularly). You'll also play a key part in helping us develop and refine our internal systems as we grow. Power Automate is the engine of everything we build. This is not a learn-on-the-job skill for this role. You need to be highly proficient in it from day one, including building custom connectors when a platform's native connector doesn't exist or doesn't expose what we need. We also build with Make, n8n, and Zapier when the work doesn't involve confidential client data. For anything sensitive, we stay inside the Microsoft ecosystem. Some of the work you'll be doing includes building scheduled AI agents that audit cases or matters across multiple connected systems, draft documents, surface findings to a human operator, and take approved actions downstream. Other projects include Teams Adaptive Cards connected to practice management systems, duplicate document detection using vector databases and semantic search, and content indexing within Microsoft. This is an ideal role for someone who loves solving problems, diving deep into Microsoft's ecosystem, and building efficient, innovative solutions. The role is not client-facing. You'll work directly with our internal team. You'll also develop basic-to-intermediate proficiency in Google Workspace tools so you can provide backup coverage for our remaining Google Workspace client during the Microsoft transition. By joining our team, you'll be learning cutting-edge AI technologies and automation tools that are shaping the future of business operations. You'll gain hands-on experience with AI-driven solutions and Microsoft-centric platforms, setting you up for long-term career growth in a tech-driven world. ============================================================ AI AT THE HEART OF WHAT WE DO ============================================================ Artificial intelligence is central to our work. On the Microsoft side, we work with Microsoft Copilot, Azure OpenAI, Azure AI Content Understanding, and Azure AI Document Intelligence. Working familiarity with these is required. We're also growing into Copilot Studio, Microsoft agent platforms (including Cowork), and Microsoft Dataverse as our clients' needs evolve. Hands-on experience here is a bonus, not a requirement. If you're strong on Power Automate, APIs, and AI fundamentals, you'll grow into these alongside us. We also occasionally touch tools outside the Microsoft ecosystem (OpenAI's ChatGPT, Anthropic's Claude, Google's Gemini, xAI's Grok, Perplexity, and others) when a client's workflow calls for it. Experience with these is a plus, not a requirement. We're looking for someone who follows AI and automation developments because they're genuinely curious, who experiments with new tools on their own time, and who gets excited when a new model, agent, or platform drops. If you find yourself researching this stuff on weekends because you find it interesting, you'll fit right in here. The application question below about the coolest thing you've used AI for is a real one. We want to hear about it. ============================================================ DAY-TO-DAY RESPONSIBILITIES ============================================================ - Build and manage automation workflows in Power Automate, Microsoft Graph API, Azure Functions, and Azure AI services for our law firm clients - Build custom connectors in Power Automate when native connectors fall short - Read and implement solutions directly from API and Microsoft developer documentation, including third-party platform documentation (practice management systems, billing, document storage, messaging, etc.) - Help build AI agents that audit, summarize, draft, and act on case data, with human-in-the-loop approval flows. We're building toward this with Copilot Studio and Microsoft agent platforms. Full Copilot Studio expertise isn't required to start, but you should be excited to grow into this work - Build duplicate detection and similarity search pipelines using vector databases, semantic search, and Microsoft indexes - Implement OCR and document intelligence workflows using Azure AI services - Build Teams Adaptive Cards as the human-in-the-loop interface for our automations, so users can approve, edit, or submit data without leaving Teams - Implement third-party tools such as FireCrawl when clients request web scraping or data extraction - Write small custom code steps in Python or JavaScript inside our flows where needed. Heavy use of AI-assisted coding is fine and expected - Work fluently with Power Automate expressions, JSON, and structured outputs - Troubleshoot, diagnose, and refine existing workflows to ensure they run smoothly and reliably - Research and recommend new Microsoft tools or techniques to improve efficiency - Document workflows and processes clearly, ensuring they're easy to replicate and maintain - Proactively identify inefficiencies and develop solutions to address them - Collaborate with the team to brainstorm and implement creative automation ideas - Stay up to date on trends in Microsoft automation and AI - Provide backup support on our remaining Google Workspace client when needed ============================================================ WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR ============================================================ - Strong proficiency in Power Automate. This is mandatory and not trainable on the job - Experience building custom connectors in Power Automate - Strong working knowledge of Azure (Azure OpenAI, Azure AI Content Understanding, Azure AI Document Intelligence, Azure Functions) and basic familiarity with Microsoft Graph - Comfortable reading and implementing APIs directly from developer documentation - Solid handle on Power Automate expressions, JSON, and structured data - Able to write small custom code steps in Python or JavaScript using AI assistance when needed - Understanding of core AI concepts including OCR, document intelligence, vector embeddings, and semantic search - Located in the Philippines - Comfortable with light team coordination: daily team huddle and sprint cycles - Fluent in English with strong spoken and written communication for frequent internal calls and chat - Proactive, detail-oriented, and enjoys solving problems - Comfortable working in a startup environment where not everything is fully established yet - Genuinely curious about AI and automation, the kind of person who tinkers with new tools and follows the space because you find it interesting, not because it's expected - Willing to learn basic-to-intermediate Google Workspace tools for backup coverage of our remaining Google Workspace client ============================================================ BONUS POINTS ============================================================ - Experience with Copilot Studio - Experience with Microsoft Dataverse as a data backend for Power Platform solutions - Experience with Microsoft agent platforms, including Cowork - Experience building with Teams Adaptive Cards - Experience with Make, n8n, or Zapier - Experience with FireCrawl or similar web-scraping tools - Experience with non-Microsoft AI APIs (OpenAI / ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, etc.) - Previous work supporting law firms or other professional services businesses - Experience providing cross-ecosystem backup or support ============================================================ COMPENSATION ============================================================ Base hourly pay will be based on your demonstrated skill level and experience. Pay will increase as you progress and as the company grows. ============================================================ HOW TO APPLY ============================================================ We're looking to hire as soon as possible, but we're prioritizing finding the right person over moving fast. Email ---------- with the subject line: Microsoft Power Platform Automation Engineer PH - [The City You Live In] In your email , include the following: - Your Resume: Attach your most recent resume - The Automation Project You're Most Proud Of: Tell us about an automation you built using Power Automate, Microsoft Graph, Azure Functions, or any platform API. Explain the problem it solved, the key parts of how it worked, and why you're most proud of it. Please also mention what data backend you used (e.g., Excel, SharePoint Lists, Dataverse, SQL, or a third-party API) and why. Bonus points if your project involved a human-in-the-loop element like Teams Adaptive Cards or custom approval routing. - The Coolest Thing You've Used AI For: Describe the most exciting or interesting way you've used AI. It doesn't need to be related to automation. Just something you're proud of or found really cool. Thank you for taking the time to read our job posting. We're excited about the possibility of working and growing together!

title: AI Automation Specialist
description: Role Purpose We have already built the foundations of an AI-driven operating system, including an internal Topweld quoting skill, a 13-machine costing model with TCO-based rates, and standardised document formats. What we now need is an automation specialist who can wire these foundations into our day-to-day Microsoft 365 environment, so that email s, invoices, and quotes move through the business with minimal manual handling. The role is delivery-focused. The successful candidate will work directly with the director, build automations inside Microsoft 365 using Power Automate and the Claude API, document every workflow as a written operating procedure, and transfer ownership to the internal team. No custom web apps, no separate databases, no bespoke development outside the Microsoft 365 stack. Priority Workstreams The role begins with three priority workstreams. The director's expectation is that each workstream is delivered, accepted, and handed over before the next begins, with a target of two weeks per workstream subject to feedback turnaround. Candidates are invited to propose a faster sequence if they can justify it. Workstream 1 – Inbox Triage and Client Communications Topweld receives RFQs, supplier correspondence, project updates, and internal traffic across two shared mailboxes ---------- ---------- is rising as the business grows, and a structured triage layer is overdue. – Deploy automated monitoring of both shared inboxes via Power Automate. – Use the Claude API to classify each incoming email into defined categories, including quote requests, supplier correspondence, active project communications, internal traffic, and noise. – Issue branded auto-acknowledgements on quote requests and new client enquiries with realistic response time expectations set by the director. – Maintain a live SharePoint register of classified email s with sender, subject, category, classification confidence, and timestamp for follow-up tracking. – Define escalation behaviour for high-priority categories and an after-hours handling rule. Acceptance Criteria – Category classification accurate on at least 90 percent of a 50 -email back-test. – Auto-acknowledgement issued within 5 minutes of receipt for any qualifying email . – Live register populated automatically, queryable, and visible to the director without manual intervention. – Written operating procedure delivered, covering monitoring, pausing, retraining, and ownership transfer. Workstream 2 – Supplier Document Intelligence Topweld receives supplier invoices, delivery dockets, and purchase order confirmations daily, currently handled manually. The objective is to lift this data out of PDFs and into structured form for reconciliation, procurement tracking, and bookkeeping handoff. – Build an extraction workflow for supplier invoices arriving via email or saved to SharePoint, using the Claude API for parsing. – Extract supplier name, invoice number, invoice date, line items, GST, freight, and total. – Write extracted data into a structured Excel workbook organised by supplier and month. – Flag any invoice with missing fields, low confidence on totals, or formatting anomalies into an exception register for manual review. – Validate the workflow against a sample of at least 20 invoices spanning our active supplier base. Acceptance Criteria – Extraction accuracy of 95 percent or higher on supplier name and invoice total. – End-to-end processing time of 10 minutes or less from inbox to Excel entry. – Exception register operating reliably so no invoice is silently misread or skipped. – Written operating procedure delivered, covering new supplier onboarding, exception review, and Excel structure maintenance. Workstream 3 – Quoting Automation Topweld already has an internal quoting skill and machine costing model covering 13 machines (press brake, fiber laser, bandsaw, guillotine, plate roller, section roller, orbital welder, lathe, mill, drill press, MIG/TIG/stick welding, auto-feeder TIG, angle grinder) with TCO-based rates. The objective is to wire this into a workflow that drafts quotes automatically from incoming RFQs and delivers them to the director for review.

job_title: AI Engineer / Autonomous Systems Builder — Claude Code + Open Models ($800–$2,500/mo DOE)
description: We are a US-based AI company running multiple brands — AI video production, AI-powered real estate technology, and a network of medical compliance clinics. We are hiring an AI Engineer who builds with autonomous agents the way developers used to build with frameworks. The honest pitch: work that used to cost us $100,000/year in dev contracts now ships in a week with the right person and the right stack. We are looking for that person. Not someone who "uses AI for coding" — someone who has internalized that the harness around the model is the actual product, and who treats Claude Code, Kimi K2, GLM, Minimax, and Qwen as a routed orchestra rather than competing chatbots. WHAT YOU'LL ACTUALLY BUILD: - Multi-agent workflows that run unsupervised overnight (planner / generator / evaluator architectures, not single-shot prompts) - Real estate data pipelines pulling MLS, HUD records, and public sources into Supabase with webhook triggers - Internal tools and dashboards for non-technical operators across our brands (we have a backlog) - Custom MCP servers when none exist for what we need - WordPress / Next.js sites cranked out fast with AI-native workflows (we have 3-4 in the pipeline right now and will pay you well to ship them) - Voice and video automation pipelines (Whisper, Seedance, fal.ai — bonus if you've touched these) - Whatever the brief is next week, because the work is varied and we move fast WHAT WE PROVIDE: - Paid access to every coding model and tool that matters — Claude Max, Kimi, GLM, Minimax, Codex, GPT, Gemini, whatever you need - Infrastructure budget (Supabase, Vercel, Cloudflare, Runpod, VPS) - Direct line to ownership — no project manager between you and the brief - Long-term recurring work across multiple brands, not one-off projects - Top performer becomes the lead and brings on junior builders under them WHAT WE DON'T WANT: - "I use ChatGPT for code" people - Anyone whose AI workflow stops at copy-paste - WordPress-only developers with no scripting depth - AI-polished cover letters that say "I am thrilled to apply for this exciting opportunity" HOW TO APPLY — READ CAREFULLY: Most applicants paste AI-generated answers to questions like these. We can tell. The candidates we hire answer like people who have shipped real systems and have the scars to prove it. Answer all nine questions below in your own words, in one sitting, without running your response through an LLM to clean it up. Short and honest beats long and polished. If your answer reads like Claude wrote it, we will assume Claude did. 1. What's the most annoying thing about Claude Code (or your daily coding agent) that you've had to work around? Be specific — what broke, what did you do? 2. Describe the last subagent, skill, slash command, or hook you built. What problem did it solve? What would you do differently next time? 3. Brief: "Pull every active MLS listing for one real estate agent, enrich each with public HUD transaction history, dump structured JSON into Supabase storage, triggered by a webhook from a form submission." Give us your rough architecture in 5–10 bullets — not the code, just how you'd stitch it. What's the hardest part? 4. Name one MCP server you've used in production (not just installed to test), and one you wish existed but doesn't. 5. Which do you reach for first for background jobs — Inngest, n8n, BullMQ, Temporal, or plain cron — and why? No wrong answer, we want your reasoning. 6. Have you actually shipped anything with Kimi K2, GLM 4.5/5, Minimax M2, Qwen 3 Coder, or any non-Anthropic frontier model? If yes — what, and how did you route between them? If no — be honest, don't make it up. 7. Tell us about a production failure. What broke, what you did, what you learned. One paragraph. 8. Send three portfolio links minimum — GitHub repos with visible commit history, live sites you built, Looms of tools you've shipped. We will look at the commit graphs. 9. One-line answers: monthly rate expectation within $800–$2,500, hours per week you can commit, time zone, and overlap with US Eastern. We read every application that answers all nine honestly. We delete the rest. BONUS (NOT REQUIRED, BUT NOTICED): - Self-hosted observability (Langfuse, Helicone, claude-code-hooks-multi-agent-observability) - Understanding of the "lethal trifecta" and prompt injection mitigation - FFmpeg / video pipeline work - Real estate, mortgage, or regulated-industry experience - Public writeups, blog posts, or X threads showing you've thought publicly about agents - GitHub commits in the last 30 days DETAILS: - Job Type: Full-Time - Salary: $800–$2,500/month based on experience demonstrated in application - Hours: Flexible, with 3–4 hours US Eastern overlap required daily

job_title: Full-Stack Developer – AI SaaS Platforms (React / Node.js / OpenAI)
description: About the Role We are a Sydney-based software development agency looking for a skilled full-stack developer to take end-to-end ownership of AI-powered SaaS platforms we are building for clients. You will be working across AI projects including multi-provider orchestration pipelines, RAG-based content generation, programmatic document processing, and full multi-tenant SaaS builds. Detailed specifications are ready to go. You will be the primary developer, working directly with our technical lead and project manager. This is a remote, exclusive role. You must be available during Australian Eastern Standard Time (AEST/AEDT) business hours. The Work You will be building full SaaS applications from scratch using React 18, Node.js, PostgreSQL, and TypeScript. The projects are heavily AI-integrated and involve real technical complexity — this is not a CRUD app role. AI Orchestration and Multi-Provider Pipelines Work includes building custom orchestration layers that chain multiple AI providers in sequence (including OpenAI, Claude, and Perplexity). You will implement pipeline logic covering parallelism, retry strategies with exponential backoff, rate limit management across providers, and streaming responses via SSE. RAG and Vector Store Architecture Projects include work with the OpenAI Responses API, file_search, and managed vector stores to generate AI content grounded in client knowledge bases. The retrieval architecture uses a multi-store design separating shared expert knowledge from per-client and per-job data — shaped by the two-vector-store-per-call constraint on the Responses API. You will build setup scripts, sync logic, metadata filtering, and the full generation pipeline. Document Processing and Assembly Work includes parsing uploaded PDF and DOCX files using Azure Document Intelligence to extract questions, tables, and document structure, then mapping AI-generated content back into the original document format without breaking layout or formatting. This is among the most technically demanding work in the engagement and a key competitive differentiator for our clients. SaaS Platform Features Projects involve full multi-tenant SaaS applications including user authentication, subscription billing via Stripe and/or Chargebee (webhooks, billing portal, feature gating by tier), knowledge base management, file uploads, admin portals, and health check engines. What You Will Be Doing Building AI-powered SaaS platforms end-to-end from detailed functional and technical specifications Implementing multi-provider AI orchestration pipelines with parallelism, retry logic, and rate limit management Setting up and managing OpenAI vector stores: file sync scripts, metadata attributes, multi-store retrieval architecture Solving document mapping challenges: parsing input documents with Azure Document Intelligence and assembling correctly formatted DOCX outputs from AI-generated content Building full SaaS platform features: auth, subscription billing, multi-tenancy, feature gating, file uploads, admin workflows Writing production-quality, well-typed TypeScript across frontend and backend Reading and building from specification documents — raising questions where specs are ambiguous or incomplete Participating in standups, providing regular progress updates, and communicating blockers early Requirements Must Have 5+ years of professional full-stack development with React and Node.js as your primary stack Strong TypeScript across frontend and backend — comfortable with type inference, generics, and type-safe ORM usage PostgreSQL with a modern ORM (Drizzle preferred, Prisma acceptable) — schema design, migrations, query optimisation Solid third-party API integration experience — authentication, webhooks, error handling OpenAI API experience, ideally the Responses API, file_search, and vector store management; if not, you must be a fast learner from documentation Azure Document Intelligence Experience parsing or generating documents programmatically (PDF, DOCX) — extracting structured data from unstructured sources or producing formatted output from code Stripe integration experience — subscription billing, webhooks, billing portal Ability to work independently from detailed specifications without needing hand-holding on every decision How to Apply Please include the following in your application: A brief summary of your relevant experience, specifically addressing the AI and document processing requirements A PDF or Google Doc link to your CV — applications without a CV will not be considered Links to projects or repositories that demonstrate your full-stack work (GitHub, portfolio, or live projects) Confirmation that you are: OK with screenshot capture software for time tracking; available during Sydney (AEST/AEDT) business hours; happy in an exclusive role with no paid or unpaid freelance work on the side; and willing to undergo a live technical assessment as part of the interview process

The more specific, the better. 5. Quick confirmation that you can work somewhere inside the hours described above. How You Use AI In your video, spend a minute or so on this. The more specific the better: - Which AI tools you use daily, weekly, and occasionally - A specific example of a build task in this role where AI saves you real time, and how you use it - A time AI gave you a wrong or bad output. How you caught it, and what you did about it - Anything you've intentionally chosen NOT to let AI do in your work, and why We're looking for real, lived examples. The specifics tell the story. A Few Questions for Your Video Take these in order, and just talk through them naturally. 1. If you came on next week and we asked you to build out our internal tooling, walk us through your first 30 days. What would you want to look at, what would you build first, and how would you d ---------- the order? 2. We hand you a vague request like "we need something to make X less painful," with no spec. What's something about building with Claude Code, MCP, or agentic workflows that's changed in the last year that you've actually adjusted your approach around?

description: ABOUT THE WARREN GROUP For more than 150 years, The Warren Group has been the Nation’s definitive source for real estate data, property records, and financial media. We serve mortgage lenders, title companies, real estate professionals, and financial institutions with comprehensive property transaction data, registry of deeds intelligence, and market analytics. We are in an active period of transformation — evolving from a traditional data and publishing business into a modern, AI-enabled data products and solutions company. This role is central to making that transformation real. ROLE OVERVIEW This is a builder’s role. The AI Enablement Analyst & Builder is the person who listens, learns, and then goes and makes things. You will talk to people across the organization — in plain business language — to understand how they work, what slows them down, and where AI or automation might help. Then you will go build the solution. You are not here to write strategy decks or run workshops. You are here to ship working solutions. At the same time, you need enough interpersonal skill and business vocabulary to earn trust from non-technical teammates and draw out the ideas they have not yet articulated. Think: part Business Analyst, part Data Analyst, part AI/Automation Engineer — all in one person. The right candidate has genuine curiosity, moves quickly from concept to working prototype, communicates with clarity in business terms, and has the technical range to build production-ready solutions without needing hand-holding. If you get energy from solving real problems and shipping things that people actually use, this role is for you. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES 1.  Discovery & Requirements Gathering You bring the listening skills of a Business Analyst. You create the conditions where colleagues feel comfortable sharing friction points, half-formed ideas, and wishlist items — then you translate those into structured, actionable requirements. Conduct structured discovery conversations with staff at all levels to surface manual, repetitive, or error-prone work Document current-state workflows using plain-language process maps, swim-lane diagrams, or simple data flow sketches Translate raw business feedback into technical requirements — capturing inputs, outputs, logic, edge cases, and success criteria Prioritize opportunities by ROI, effort, and strategic alignment — communicating trade-offs clearly to the CEO and leadership Build enough trust with each team that they proactively bring you their next idea 2.  Build, Automate & Implement This is the core of the role. Once a problem is defined and a solution is scoped, you build it — not hand it off. Design and build AI-powered workflows, automated pipelines, and intelligent tools using Python, APIs, LLMs, and low-code/no-code platforms Implement automation across business functions: data operations, sales ops, finance, marketing, editorial, and client reporting Integrate AI capabilities (e.g., LLM-based classification, extraction, summarization, generation) into existing workflows Connect systems via APIs — internal databases, CRMs, SaaS tools, and data platforms Deploy, monitor, and iterate on solutions — you own the work until it is stable and adopted Write clean, maintainable code and document your work so the team can understand and extend it 3.  Data Analysis & Operational Reporting You think in data. You can pull, shape, and analyze data to validate assumptions, measure impact, and surface insights — and you communicate those findings in plain business language. Query operational databases and data pipelines using SQL to understand data structure, quality, and volume Build lightweight dashboards and reports that give leadership real-time visibility into operational KPIs and initiative progress Conduct pre/post analysis to measure the impact of process changes and automation deployments Identify data quality issues that block automation or distort reporting — and fix them Support the data and technology teams with field-level validation, deduplication, and quality assurance workflows 4.
